investigation.title: project-agent-a2a-roundtrip: Planner agent halts after list_agents — send_to_agent never invoked, reviewer receives zero events
investigation.summary: The desktop-release eval for project-agent-a2a-roundtrip failed because the planner agent called list_agents successfully but never proceeded to call send_to_agent, leaving sendToAgentUsed=false, delivered=false, targetMatches=false, and reviewerAckObserved=false. The reviewer agent received zero events and its event-wait timed out after 120 000 ms, confirming no message was ever dispatched to it.
investigation.rootCause: The planner agent stopped its tool-use sequence after list_agents and did not invoke send_to_agent. Because send_to_agent was never called, no message was routed to the reviewer agent, the reviewer event stream received nothing (reviewerEventCount=0), and the full A2A roundtrip could not complete. The precise reason the planner halted — whether a missing or mis-registered send_to_agent tool, a model decision not to call it, a runtime dispatch error, or a probe harness defect in runProjectAgentToAgentRoundtrip — cannot be determined from the supplied evidence alone. This is an eval-layer failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet.

(Lower evidence weight) A permissions or capability gap in the desktop-release environment that blocks the send_to_agent tool from being granted to the planner agent instance, even though basic tool use and chat streaming work.

investigation.title: project-agent-subagent-roundtrip: Post-turn context hydration timed out — contextUtilization and subagentContextCount remained zero after subagent completed
investigation.summary: The eval confirmed that the subagent was spawned, ran to completion, and returned the expected marker (subagentSpawned=true, subagentCompleted=true, subagentReturnedMarker=true), but the subsequent context-hydration poll timed out after 45 000 ms without ever observing a non-zero contextUtilization or subagentContextCount. The two failing assertions — contextUtilization expected >= 0.000001 but got 0, and subagentContextCount expected >= 1 but got 0 — are therefore a post-turn context-read failure, not a subagent execution failure.
investigation.rootCause: After the subagent task turn completed successfully, the probe's context-hydration step polled for contextUtilization and subagentContextCount to become non-zero but received zero for both fields throughout the entire 45 000 ms window (contextError: "Timed out after 45000ms waiting for expected value"). The root cause is uncertain between two candidates: (1) the desktop-release runtime is not writing or exposing context-usage data for the parent agent instance after a subagent turn completes, or (2) the probe's context-read path (runProjectSubagentRoundtrip in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs) is polling the wrong endpoint, session, or agent-instance identifier and therefore never sees the populated context. The sibling check project-agent-a2a-roundtrip also failed with a distinct multi-agent coordination failure, but its failure message shares no overlap with this one and the verifier context flags likelySharedDependencyFailure=false, so the two failures are treated as independent.

possibleCauses: (Most likely) The desktop-release runtime does not populate or expose context-usage/contents for the parent agent instance after a foreground subagent turn, causing the probe's context-hydration poll to time out at 45 000 ms with zero values for contextUtilization and subagentContextCount.

(Equally plausible) The context-hydration polling logic inside runProjectSubagentRoundtrip is querying the wrong identifier (e.g., the child run's context rather than the parent agent instance's context, or a stale session reference), so the correct data exists but is never observed by the probe.

(Lower likelihood) A latency regression in the context-hydration API causes the data to become available after the 45 000 ms poll window closes, making the timeout a timing issue rather than a missing-data issue.

(Lower likelihood) The toolsContextContainsTask=false value indicates the task tool is not reflected in the tools-context view after the turn; this could be a separate serialization or indexing gap in the context-hydration layer that also prevents contextUtilization and subagentContextCount from being populated.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (the resource quota for peer-pod VMs is exhausted or the allocatable count is zero), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained Unschedulable for ~141–146 seconds across all three checks, which is the direct cause of the eval failure. This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact to production end-users cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

Preemption was also ruled out ("No preemption victims found"). investigations.title: project-agent-a2a-roundtrip: Planner agent halts after list_agents — send_to_agent never invoked, reviewer receives zero events
investigations.summary: The desktop-release eval for project-agent-a2a-roundtrip failed because the planner agent called list_agents successfully but never proceeded to call send_to_agent, leaving sendToAgentUsed=false, delivered=false, targetMatches=false, and reviewerAckObserved=false. The reviewer agent received zero events and its event-wait timed out after 120 000 ms, confirming no message was ever dispatched to it.
investigations.rootCause: The planner agent stopped its tool-use sequence after list_agents and did not invoke send_to_agent. Because send_to_agent was never called, no message was routed to the reviewer agent, the reviewer event stream received nothing (reviewerEventCount=0), and the full A2A roundtrip could not complete. The precise reason the planner halted — whether a missing or mis-registered send_to_agent tool, a model decision not to call it, a runtime dispatch error, or a probe harness defect in runProjectAgentToAgentRoundtrip — cannot be determined from the supplied evidence alone. This is an eval-layer failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet.

possibleCauses: (Highest evidence weight) send_to_agent is not available in the planner agent's tool registry at runtime — list_agents is present and used, but send_to_agent may not be registered or exposed to the planner in the desktop-release environment, causing the model to stop after discovery with no tool to call.

(Medium evidence weight) The planner agent's model decided not to call send_to_agent after receiving the list_agents result — a model-behavior or prompt/instruction issue in the probe harness that does not force the send step, rather than a missing tool.

(Lower evidence weight, corroborated by sibling failure) A shared cross-agent communication or context-routing layer defect affecting both A2A dispatch (this check) and subagent context hydration (project-agent-subagent-roundtrip) — both multi-agent coordination checks fail while all single-agent checks pass.

(Lower evidence weight) A permissions or capability gap in the desktop-release environment that blocks the send_to_agent tool from being granted to the planner agent instance, even though basic tool use and chat streaming work.

investigations.title: project-agent-subagent-roundtrip: Post-turn context hydration timed out — contextUtilization and subagentContextCount remained zero after subagent completed
investigations.summary: The eval confirmed that the subagent was spawned, ran to completion, and returned the expected marker (subagentSpawned=true, subagentCompleted=true, subagentReturnedMarker=true), but the subsequent context-hydration poll timed out after 45 000 ms without ever observing a non-zero contextUtilization or subagentContextCount. The two failing assertions — contextUtilization expected >= 0.000001 but got 0, and subagentContextCount expected >= 1 but got 0 — are therefore a post-turn context-read failure, not a subagent execution failure.
investigations.rootCause: After the subagent task turn completed successfully, the probe's context-hydration step polled for contextUtilization and subagentContextCount to become non-zero but received zero for both fields throughout the entire 45 000 ms window (contextError: "Timed out after 45000ms waiting for expected value"). The root cause is uncertain between two candidates: (1) the desktop-release runtime is not writing or exposing context-usage data for the parent agent instance after a subagent turn completes, or (2) the probe's context-read path (runProjectSubagentRoundtrip in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs) is polling the wrong endpoint, session, or agent-instance identifier and therefore never sees the populated context. The sibling check project-agent-a2a-roundtrip also failed with a distinct multi-agent coordination failure, but its failure message shares no overlap with this one and the verifier context flags likelySharedDependencyFailure=false, so the two failures are treated as independent.

possibleCauses: (Most likely) The desktop-release runtime does not populate or expose context-usage/contents for the parent agent instance after a foreground subagent turn, causing the probe's context-hydration poll to time out at 45 000 ms with zero values for contextUtilization and subagentContextCount.

(Equally plausible) The context-hydration polling logic inside runProjectSubagentRoundtrip is querying the wrong identifier (e.g., the child run's context rather than the parent agent instance's context, or a stale session reference), so the correct data exists but is never observed by the probe.

(Lower likelihood) A latency regression in the context-hydration API causes the data to become available after the 45 000 ms poll window closes, making the timeout a timing issue rather than a missing-data issue.

(Lower likelihood) The toolsContextContainsTask=false value indicates the task tool is not reflected in the tools-context view after the turn; this could be a separate serialization or indexing gap in the context-hydration layer that also prevents contextUtilization and subagentContextCount from being populated.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (the resource quota for peer-pod VMs is exhausted or the allocatable count is zero), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained Unschedulable for ~141–146 seconds across all three checks, which is the direct cause of the eval failure. This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact to production end-users cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] The kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource quota on the 2 eligible nodes is fully consumed by existing running peer-pod VMs, leaving zero allocatable capacity for new pods at the time of the eval run.

[Likely] A node affinity or node selector on the remote agent pod spec restricts scheduling to a specific node pool or label set that only matches 2 of the 6 nodes, and those 2 nodes are simultaneously capacity-exhausted.
[Possible] The 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes are in a degraded or cordoned state that prevents new allocations even though they appear schedulable by node count.

[Possible] A recent scale-down or node eviction reduced the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes below the level needed to absorb concurrent probe requests, causing all three sibling checks to contend for the same exhausted pool.

[Less likely] The kata.peerpods.io/vm resource advertised capacity was reduced (e.g., via a device plugin configuration change) without a corresponding reduction in active VM workloads, creating an over-committed state.
